artworks.title: In Prison
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink on wove paper
artworks.description: The image shows an illustration of two people. One is seated on a chair, their face buried in their hand. The other is standing beside them, leaning slightly forward with one hand on the seated person's shoulder. The seated individual has medium-length hair and is dressed in a shirt and pants. The standing person has neatly styled hair pulled back and is wearing a long dress or robe. The background is plain with some texture on the paper. The words "In Prison" and a signature "W. Soul" are inscribed at the bottom of the image.

artworks.title: Studies of Figural Groups
artworks.description: This image features a sketch with multiple vignettes showing individuals in various interactions and settings. One vignette shows a man leaning against a building, another shows two men conversing outside a door, a woman walking, a man walking with a sack, two women seated and one writing, and a couple engaged in conversation. The sketches are drawn in pencil on plain paper, without color, with some surrounding notes and writing.

artworks.title: Long Island, New York
artworks.description: The image shows a serene landscape viewed from an elevated position. Close to us is a patch of grass and low foliage with hints of a trail. Beyond this area lies a calm body of water reflecting the surroundings. In the middle distance, a small house is nestled amongst trees, with a few figures near the water's edge. The horizon is lined with trees of varying heights and densities. The sketch employs short, curved lines and shading for texture and depth to the foliage and clouds. The color palette is monochromatic, created solely by pencil lines and shading, resulting in a soft, tranquil visual impact.

artworks.title: Valley with River and Mountains
artworks.description: The image shows an elevated view of a landscape with mountain ranges stretching across the horizon. The drawing is done in a simple pencil sketch style with light strokes. The color palette is monochromatic, using natural tones. In the foreground, there are small structures, trees, and fields. In the distance, a body of water can be seen with tiny boats.

artworks.title: Le brodeur
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image depicts a man seated in a side profile, engaged in embroidery work. He has distinctive facial features and dark hair styled with a middle parting. The man wears a dark high-collared shirt under a checkered jacket. He holds an embroidery tool and frame with threads visible. The background shows a lightly sketched design resembling a publication page with the heading "MONOMANES" at the top.

artworks.title: New York Street Scene
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum exchange through a gift of Rear Adm. E.H.C. Leutze, 1960)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an urban street scene featuring a three-story building with balconies and a street lamp. Various architectural details are depicted, such as windows, doors, awnings, and laundry hanging from the balconies. Two figures are shown standing near a doorway. The pencil work captures textures of bricks, wood, and fabric, conveying a sense of age and vibrancy. The composition includes a street lamp as the focal point, along with street-level details like barrels and crates near the building entrance.

artworks.title: Self-Portrait
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase through a gift of Mrs. J.L.M. Curry, 1979)
artworks.description: The image is a portrait of a man's head and upper shoulders in a monochromatic style. His round face has shadows around his eyes, which are looking straight ahead. He has thick, slightly wavy hair styled away from his face and a well-groomed mustache. The background is plain and dark, contrasting with the lighter tones of the man's face. The artist's signature and the date, 1896, are found in the lower left corner.

artworks.title: David Burns's Cottage and the Washington Monument
artworks.medium: watercolor over graphite on wove paper

artworks.title: Plate Number 11. Walking
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a grid-format motion study capturing the movement of a figure walking. The image shows sequential stages of the figure as it moves laterally and towards the camera. The controlled outdoor setting features even lighting, consistent spacing, and vertical lines in the background.

artworks.title: Plate Number 63. Running at full speed
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a grid displaying sequential frames capturing the motion of a running figure. The grid contains side profile shots showing different stages of the running stride, with a backdrop featuring a grid pattern. The second row shows the figure from behind, offering a different perspective of the stride. The images are in grayscale and focus on documenting the mechanics of human motion, emphasizing the dynamics of movement.

artworks.title: Plate Number 101. Turning, ascending stairs and waving hand
Plate Number 143. Descending stairs, a cup and saucer in right hand
artworks.description: This is a series of 24 black-and-white panels showing the movement of a figure in a white garment ascending and descending stairs while holding a cup. The panels are arranged in two rows. The background is plain and lined. The figure is captured in different phases of movement, from standing still to walking on stairs. The lighting highlights the contours and folds of the garment. The series presents a study of motion captured through photography, emphasizing movement's grace and fluidity.

artworks.title: Plate Number 155. Jumping, running straight high jump
artworks.description: This is a series of images showing a sequence of movements resembling a jump and walk. The collage includes multiple frames arranged in a grid format capturing different phases of the action. Each frame delineates a fraction of the action, showing subtle variations in posture and position. The sequential images suggest a study of motion, focusing on the nuances of physical movements. The background is a consistent structured setting, emphasizing the fluidity and continuity of movement.

artworks.title: Plate Number 162. Jumping, standing broad jump
artworks.description: The image is a sequential set of photographs of a man performing a jump, capturing different phases of his movement. The man starts standing upright with raised arms, goes through bending, taking off, being airborne, and landing positions. His facial features are not clearly visible. He has short hair and is wearing tight undergarments. The setting is indoor with a parallel lined surface backdrop. The floor is plain, with no other visible objects. The background remains consistent throughout the sequence.

artworks.title: Plate Number 170. Jumping from stone to stone across a brook
artworks.description: This is a photograph of sequential movements over an obstacle. The image consists of twenty-four separate black and white frames arranged in a grid, depicting the motion sequence of a subject wrapped in fabric interacting with a large spherical object on the ground. Each row shows a continuous motion with different poses demonstrating balance, momentum, and motion, captured near a textured backdrop. The lighting and tones highlight a vintage and experimental photographic style, providing insights into movement and form.

artworks.title: Plate Number 180. Stepping on and over a chair
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a sequence of movement study. The image features two rows of grid-like background photographs, capturing stages of a subject climbing onto and stepping down from a stool. Each photograph in the sequence shows a moment in time of this motion. The frames are arranged systematically to give a clear view of this continuous motion, with the top series showing the movement from the side and the bottom series from behind.

artworks.title: Plate Number 186. Hopping on right foot
artworks.description: This is a photograph of sequential movements captured in a grid format. The image displays a series of photographs arranged in three rows, showing the progression of motion in small incremental steps. Each row illustrates a different angle. The background shows a consistent setting with vertical lines and features. The photographs capture each pose in great detail.

artworks.title: Plate Number 196.Two women dancing a waltz
Plate Number 237. Sitting down on a chair and opening a fan
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a sequence showing the motion of a person interacting with a fan and a chair. The image comprises multiple frames laid out in a grid format, capturing detailed stages of movement. The top row illustrates a person holding a fan and transitioning from standing to sitting on a chair. The lower row continues the motion captured from a rear view, depicting the figure's movements from standing to sitting while holding the fan. The setting includes a gridded backdrop emphasizing the motion sequence, highlighting subtle changes in posture and position throughout the frames. This photographic study serves to analyze and understand movement through sequential imaging.

artworks.title: Plate Number 315. Heaving a 20-lb. rock
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a series of frames capturing the motion of a person throwing a ball. The series consists of multiple black and white frames arranged in a grid pattern, illustrating the sequential movement involved in the act of throwing. Each frame captures slight variations in posture, depicting the dynamic transition from a standing position, to the act of hurling a ball, and the subsequent finishing pose. The background is composed of vertical lines, suggesting a stationary backdrop that highlights the progressive motion in each image. The sequential nature of the images suggests an early study in motion and movement photography, capturing the nuances of physical dynamics.

artworks.title: Plate Number 344. Striking a blow with right hand
artworks.description: This is a photograph of sequential motion studies. The image captures a sequence of twelve black and white photographs arranged in a grid. Each photograph shows the progression of movement. The background is a grid used for analysis of movement. The figure remains consistent in each frame, allowing for detailed observation of the motion.

artworks.title: Plate Number 350. Fencing
artworks.description: This is a series of images featuring a fencing sequence. The grid of smaller frames shows two individuals engaging in fencing movements. The figures showcase various combat poses like advancing, parrying, and attacking. The setting appears to be an enclosed space with a textured backdrop. The monochromatic images emphasize the forms and muscles of the figures, highlighting the physical exertion of the movements.

artworks.title: Plate Number 359. Charging bayonet
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a series of sequential images capturing movement. The image shows a series of frames arranged in a grid, each depicting the motion in a consistent setting. The background is a lined or gridded curtain or wall that aids in analyzing movement. The photos are likely part of a study in locomotion, showing movement through various stages across the grid. The frames illustrate a change in position that can be analyzed for differences in posture and motion over time, captured in documentary-style photography.

artworks.title: Plate Number 379. Carpenter, planing a board
artworks.description: This is a series of sequential photographs showing a figure using a tool on a piece of wood. The photos progress from left to right, capturing different stages of the action. The setting appears to be an interior space, and the lighting is even without harsh shadows.
